fields.corePath: A saree reseller who sells on WhatsApp and Instagram opens the site. Step 1, she clicks Open my order book — this makes a book for her on the spot with a six-letter code, no email, no password, and the code goes in the URL so her browser remembers it. Step 2, she clicks Add order and fills the form: customer first name, city, which saree (she can pick from her uploaded catalogue or just type "red Kanjivaram with gold border"), the price, and how much advance she has taken. Step 3, she saves, and the order lands in the Booked column. Step 4, as things move she drags the card, or on a phone taps the card and picks the next stage: Booked, Paid, With tailor, Dispatched, Delivered. Step 5, when she taps Dispatched it asks for the courier and the tracking number, and gives her a WhatsApp message already written — "Your red Kanjivaram is dispatched, DTDC, tracking 9xxxxxxx" — which she copies into the customer's chat. Step 6, the strip at the top always shows money in, money still owed, and how many are sitting with the tailor.
fields.knownGaps:
The order book is protected by nothing except the secret code in the URL. If she forwards that link to somebody, they have her whole book. I know this is the weakest part and I have written it on the page in plain words rather than pretending. Catalogue photos upload to Cloudinary on a free plan; past about 25 photos it starts rejecting them and the error message it shows is the raw one from Cloudinary, which is useless to her. Amounts are rupees only, no paise, and I round off — two of my early testers sell in round numbers anyway. There is no search, so once she is past around 60 orders she is scrolling the columns. Deleting an order is permanent with no undo and no confirm dialog, which has already cost one tester an order she had to retype. The WhatsApp message is copy-and-paste, it does not actually send — I have not done the Business API. None of these sit on the path above; adding an order, moving it through the five stages and getting the dispatch message all work.

Thanks for reading this far — Ishita Rane (ishita@sareesaath.in)
